title: 大成建設、手形やめ現金払いに　中小への支払い80日短縮
extracted_text:
大成建設 など大手ゼネコンが協力会社の中小企業を対象に約束手形による支払いをやめ、現金払いに切り替える。支払も早め、現金を受け取るまでの期間を短くする。取引先の資金繰りを支えて倒産を防ぎ、施工体制の安定につなげる。

大成建設は7月の請求分から資本金3億円以下の協力会社を対象に、現金払いに一本化する。これまでは現場作業員の労務費のみ現金払いで、材料費や外注費は現金と満期60日間の手形を併用していた。

あわせて材料・外注費の支払日を労務費と同じ翌月5日にそろえる。発行が翌月25日となる手形に比べ、現金を受け取るまでの期間が80日間短くなる。

手形の廃止で従来よりも多くの現金が必要になるものの、手元資金でまかなえるとみる。今回対象とする資本金3億円以下は同社の協力企業の約9割に当たる。それ以外の取引先に関しても今後の状況を踏まえ、支払い条件の改善を検討する。

大林組 は4月以降に締結する全ての協力企業との取引契約で、全額現金払いに切り替えを始めた。これまでは一部の取引で満期60日間の手形を使っていた。現行の契約が終了し、新たな契約を結び直す際に現金払いに一本化する。

大手ゼネコンが手形払いをやめるのは、取引先の資金繰りを改善して倒産を防ぐためだ。東京商工リサーチによると、2025年度に発生した建設業の倒産は2047件と前の年度比5%増え、12年ぶりの高水準だった。人手不足や資材価格の上昇が響いた。

経営に行き詰まる下請け企業が増えれば、ゼネコンの施工体制にも悪影響が出かねない。資金繰りを支援することで自社工事に関わる技能労働者の確保を後押しする。

政府や業界団体からの要請もきっかけとなった。国土交通省は建設業法の順守を求めるガイドラインで、協力企業への代金の支払いはできる限り現金とするよう求める。日本建設業連合会（日建連）は自主行動計画で会員各社に対し、現金払いの比率を高めるよう呼びかける。

ゼネコンの取引の多くは建設業法が適用され、1月施行の中小受託取引適正化法（取適法）の対象にはなっていない。取適法では手形払いを原則禁止している。

手形払いを巡っては27年3月末で紙の手形が廃止され、オンライン形式の手形である電子記録債権（でんさい）に完全移行する。中小事業者では紙の手形取引が商慣習として残り、でんさいの普及が遅れている。こうした状況を踏まえ、大成建設や大林組は紙とでんさいの両方の使用をやめて現金払いに一本化する。

translated_text:
Taisei Construction and other major general contractors are switching from promissory notes to cash payments for small and medium subcontractors. They will also accelerate payments, shortening the time until cash is received. This aims to support the cash flow of business partners and prevent bankruptcies, leading to a stable construction system.

Taisei Construction will unify to cash payments for cooperating companies with capital of 300 million yen or less starting from July invoices. Previously, only labor costs for on-site workers were paid in cash, while materials and subcontracting fees used a combination of cash and 60-day promissory notes.

Additionally, payment dates for materials and subcontracting fees will be aligned with labor costs, set for the 5th of the following month. Compared to promissory notes issued on the 25th of the following month, the period to receive cash will be shortened by 80 days.

While abandoning promissory notes will require more cash on hand, the company believes its available funds can cover this. The capital threshold of 300 million yen or less applies to approximately 90% of its cooperating companies. Regarding other business partners, the company will consider improving payment terms based on future conditions.

Obayashi Kiso began switching to full cash payments for all new contracts with cooperating companies from April onward. Previously, some transactions used 60-day promissory notes. The transition occurs when current contracts expire and new agreements are being signed.

Major general contractors are abandoning promissory note payments to improve cash flow and prevent bankruptcies among business partners. According to Tokyo Shoko Research, construction industry bankruptcies in fiscal year 2025 reached 2,047 cases, a 5% increase from the previous year and the highest level in 12 years. Labor shortages and rising material costs have contributed to this trend.

When subcontractors face business difficulties, it can negatively impact general contractors' construction systems. Supporting cash flow helps ensure skilled workers for their own construction projects.

The shift was also prompted by requests from the government and industry associations. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism's guidelines under the Construction Industry Law call for cash payments to subcontractors whenever possible. The Japan Federation of Construction Contractors has urged member companies to increase their cash payment ratio in voluntary action plans.

Most construction transactions are governed by the Construction Industry Law and are not subject to the Subcontractor Transaction Properization Law, which took effect in January and generally prohibits promissory note payments. 

Regarding promissory notes, paper notes will be abolished by the end of March 2027, with full transition to electronic records (densai). Paper note transactions remain common practice among small and medium businesses, and adoption of densai has been slow. In response, Taisei Construction and Obayashi Kiso are eliminating both paper notes and densai entirely in favor of cash payments.
title_en: Taisei Construction Ditches Promissory Notes for Cash Payments - SMEs to Receive Funds 80 Days Earlier
